scope: Camelot and Aerodrome SE compatibility; not excluded Balancer DETFs or deferred Slipstream

facts.finding: Current deployment rejects stableSwap pools. Projection work need only preserve the existing volatile-pool acceptance.
Current deployment rejects stable pools. This is an existing policy, not a new proposed allowlist.

Actual volatile protocol LP mint uses the Camelot sqrt and ownerFeeShare denominator. The shared ConstProdUtils helper special-cases owner shares 16666/16667 as Uniswap, so a general Camelot projection must reproduce the actual pool formula instead of blindly substituting constants.

Swap/zap execution passes the current vault feeTo as Camelot referrer. Factory referrersFeeShare can cause input tokens to leave pool reserves; projecting all swap fees as retained reserves is not generally exact.

Current post-zap checkpoint code uses the pre-operation indexSource snapshot and writes the known/opposing values under token0/token1 without reordering. The analogous withdrawal block starts at line859. This differs from the updated Uniswap V2 quote model. A simple source clone is insufficient; compare actual sequences in both asset orders with nonzero usage fees before choosing the correction.
Existing CamelotV2NativeSYTest is the canonical real registry/proxy fixture for adding focused projection or checkpoint regressions; keep existing tests.

next: Camelot 19-case validation is complete. Assess remaining Aerodrome compatibility independently.

additional_review.finding: The existing _sortReservesStruct already maps a zero known token to token0. No sorting-default change is needed.
The LP-to-pair preview branch computes amountOut but does not return it, then falls through to InvalidRoute. A fifth actual-proxy regression and isolated missing-return correction are prepared.
The exact-output asset withdrawal transfers all actual zap proceeds. The projection draft preserves this behavior rather than assuming it transfers only the requested minimum.

Aero compounds claimed fees plus saved excess, pays usage fees in LP tokens and keeps SE supply unchanged. A future projection can reuse the existing compound math but must track pool LP fee indexes and excess across transitions.

Existing _previewCompoundState models post-compound reserves and LP supply, with reusable internal _previewApplyProportionalDeposit/_previewApplySwapDepositWithFee. It currently loads live claimable fees/excess, so repeated projected transitions need state-backed inputs instead of repeatedly rereading live state.
